"Don't do this if you're driving, in the water, operating machinery, or otherwise need to be attending to yourself or other people." follows it and carries them, so 'safe place' reads as physical safety there. The sentence it replaces did not carry the exclusions or 'physically' either, and is no narrower or broader than the draft, so nothing is lost against the text as it stands. The author may still want to hear that the frame doubles. T14/T15: the writer's ledger evidence for these says the draft 'puts back the author's own point that Emulate dropped' and 'puts back the author's words or meaning'; that is template wording that does not fit this card (the draft is Emulate's sentence unchanged and puts nothing back). All other rows (T01, T03-T13, T16-T25, T27-T29, C01-C04) are not happening: one plain imperative, no stake, scene, image, aftercare, colon, tic word, closer or invented first-person fact; 'this' is the practice the section prepares, the same referent as in the sentence replaced (C02). "E36/E41 heavy second person" (10.0 'you' per 100 of my words) accepted: it is the arithmetic of a ten-word sentence with one "you're"; the replaced sentence has two second-person words ('yourself', 'you'), the draft one, and the guide addresses the reader as 'you' throughout.
